content.title: About
content.content: Ruffled potato chips with barbecue flavor are thinly sliced potatoes fried until crisp and coated with a smoky, sweet‑spicy seasoning blend typical of barbecue: smoked pepper, paprika, onion and garlic.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The ruffled shape increases surface area, allowing the seasoning to cling better.
Barbecue flavor originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a way to mimic smoked meat aromas.
Potato chips became a popular snack in 1853 after the invention of a mechanical slicer.
There are over 200 chip flavors worldwide, with barbecue consistently ranking in the top five.
Most manufacturers use a polyphosphate solution to preserve crunchiness.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Chips provide carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: Vitamin C content
items.content: Despite frying, a small amount of vitamin C remains in the potato.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Potassium and iron are present, supporting muscle function and blood formation.

items.title: Antioxidants in spices
items.content: Paprika and smoked pepper contain carotenoids with antioxidant properties.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Chips often contain a lot of salt, which can raise blood pressure when eaten frequently.

items.title: Fats and calories
items.content: Deep‑frying makes the product calorie‑dense and rich in saturated and trans fats.

items.title: Allergy to potato or spices
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to potato or added flavorings.

items.title: Acrylamide
items.content: High‑temperature frying can produce acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound, so moderation is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy chips as a standalone snack, toss them into salads, use as a crunchy topping for soups, or incorporate into party appetizers. Opt for lower‑salt versions when possible.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep chips in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from light. After opening, transfer to an airtight container to maintain crispness.
